Speed-dependent emissions with emis_speed

Source: vignettes/speed.Rmd
speed.Rmd

Why speed-dependent emission factors?

Local emission factors (for instance the CETESB values used in Brazil) are usually measured over a driving cycle and reported as a single number per age. The EMEP/EEA guidebook provides speed curves for the same technologies. ef_ldv_scaled() and ef_hdv_scaled() combine both: the EMEP/EEA curve gives the shape as a function of the average speed, and it is rescaled so that at the speed of the local driving cycle (SDC) it reproduces the local emission factor.

Estimating an inventory for many streets and hours with these curves used to be very slow, because the R equations were interpreted once per street, hour and age. emis_speed() compiles the equations to a tiny stack machine and evaluates them in an OpenMP C kernel (src/e_speed.c), grouping the ages that share the same equation.

Scaling a local emission factor by speed 

library(vein)
library(units)
#> udunits database from /usr/share/xml/udunits/udunits2.xml

# local (CETESB) emission factors for passenger cars, 40 ages
CO <- ef_cetesb(p = "CO", veh = "PC_G", year = 2018, agemax = 40, full = TRUE)

# scale the EMEP/EEA curve so that at SDC = 34.12 km/h it gives the local EF
lef <- ef_ldv_scaled(
  dfcol = CO$CO,
  v = "PC", t = "4S", cc = "<=1400", f = "G",
  eu = CO$EqEuro_PC, p = "CO"
)
length(lef)
#> [1] 40

Running the inventory

emis_speed() needs the vehicle flow by age (veh), the link lengths (lkm), the number of hours and speeds. It returns the emissions by street and hour and, optionally, the totals by age and hour.

S <- 200 # streets
A <- 40  # ages
H <- 24  # hours

veh <- matrix(100, nrow = S, ncol = A)
lkm <- set_units(rep(1, S), "km")
speed <- Speed(matrix(rep(c(10, 30, 50, 80), length.out = S * H), S, H))
profile <- matrix(1, 24, 1)

E <- emis_speed(
  veh = veh,
  lkm = lkm,
  ef = lef,
  speed = speed,
  profile = profile,
  by_age = TRUE,
  nt = 2
)

# emissions by street and hour
dim(E$streets)
#> [1] 200  24
# total emissions by age and hour
dim(E$veh)
#> [1] 40 24
round(sum(E$streets), 1)
#> [1] 200577240

The result is equivalent to the reference implementation emis() (to machine precision) but considerably faster, which makes country-scale hourly inventories feasible. The detailed workflow, with CETESB emission factors and a 168 h week, is implemented in the brazil_bu_speed project:

get_project(directory = tempdir(), case = "brazil_bu_speed")
